items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: That's the first place, in her house, that I heard Pop's West End Blues

ctx.x: But we didn't have the records. We couldn't afford them. And there was a lady that -- well, our people thought it was the wrong house for us to be in. They called it like the house of ill repute, you know. The only thing she did was sold drinks because that's a dry county,

still is, and she just sold drinks. But she had every record of everybody. That's the first place, in her house, that I heard Pop's West End Blues and that's the first time I'd heard Coon-Saunders' 'Sluefoot'. They made a thing called Sluefoot, was the big thing, I loved the saxophone playing in that, you know.

So we'd go there and listen to all of her records because she had everything and until our parents found out what we were doing, see, so they just thought that was the wrong kind of house for us to be in, you know what I mean. But it really didn't stop us because, you know, we would say, 'Okay,' but we'd sneak back in there and listen to them. She ended up marrying my cousin. He wasn't a musician. And I think she's still alive. He told me that she lives in Fort Worth and she's -- well, she would be pretty old…
